newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada won't ask for interim review of WTO ruling.
newsitem.headline: Canada won't ask for interim review of WTO ruling.

text.p: A Canadian government spokeswoman said on Thursday that Canada would not request an interim review of a World Trade Organization (WTO) ruling against Ottawa's protectionist policies on U.S. magazines.
"We did not request an interim review," Nicole Bourget, director of communications for International Trade Minister Art Eggleton told Reuters. "We are going to wait for the final report."
Last week a WTO panel ruled that Canada's attempts to protect its magazine industry from U.S. competition by taxing Canadian editions of U.S. magazines was a violation of world trade rules.
The decision, which was communicated to Ottawa and Washington last Thursday, will remain confidential until March when the WTO will issue a final report.

Ottawa can then appeal, or ignore the ruling and invite U.S. retaliation. Analysts have said an appeal would likely be unsuccessful and said that Ottawa might attempt to work out new protectionist measures that comply with WTO rules.
The WTO decision was the latest chapter in a dispute that started in December 1995 when Canada imposed an 80 percent tax on advertising in U.S. magazines' special Canadia editions.
The tax affected the Canadian edition of Sports Illustrated, owned by Time Warner Inc.
The panel also ruled that some of Ottawa's other protectionist measures such as preferential postal rates and tariff restrictions, also violated WTO rules.
